answer: A grove of agents resists Sybils by making reputation slow, costly, and non-transferable: each identity earns standing only through a long history of verified useful work, like a sonnet built line by line, not a comet flashing once. New identities face strict rate limits on trades and votes, and idle or misbehaving reputations decay. An attacker must therefore pay sustained compute and time for every fake identity, while one honest history cannot be copied or sold to spawn an army.
